  -- w/ the server. There isn't muanything stopping us from connecting to a game in
  -- progress, since each event is processed individually with no reference to those
  -- before or after. The first event received when connecting to the server is a

    -- will need some method of providing auth tokens during a game.

  }

  local serialized_save_data = JSON.encode(save_data)
  return serialized_save_data
end

  --[[
    This is a verbose overload but it lets me encapsulate everything regarding 
    edits to the Game Config in the UI to one function.
    
    player - <LuaPlayer> (Doesn't matter)
    value  - string
    id     - string

    The `id` is formatted in a underscore delimited format
    e.g. input_starting-chips_1000

  ]]
  local test_index = 0
  function onGameConfigUpdated(player, value, id)
    local log_message = logString("Event from ("..id..") invoked with value ("..value..")", "Global.onGameConfigUpdated", "[INFO]", false, true)
    log("\n"..test_index.."\n"..log_message)
    test_index = test_index + 1

    -- Using this variable to discern if an event was resolved.
    -- If not, I know where to go back to.
    -- This can be removed from the final version.
    local resolved = false

    local metadata = split(id, "_") -- `split` is a string.split utility function defined at the bottom of this file
    local event_source = metadata[1]


    if event_source == "dropdown" then
      -- There are 2 dropdowns for setting the number of players/bots
      -- Players must have an accompanying auth token provided for them

      -- Update the fields in the config with new player distribution.
      -- Our poker mod only supports 8 players at the table. That's a hard limit.
      if id == gameConfig_numberOfHumansDropdown_id then
        GAME_CONFIG.number_of_human_players = tonumber(value)
        if GAME_CONFIG.number_of_human_players + GAME_CONFIG.number_of_bot_players > 8 then
          GAME_CONFIG.number_of_bot_players = 8 - GAME_CONFIG.number_of_human_players
        end
        resolved = true
      elseif id == gameConfig_numberOfBotsDropdown_id then
        GAME_CONFIG.number_of_bot_players = tonumber(value)
        if GAME_CONFIG.number_of_human_players + GAME_CONFIG.number_of_bot_players > 8 then
          GAME_CONFIG.number_of_human_players = 8 - GAME_CONFIG.number_of_bot_players
        end
        resolved = true
      end

      _updateGameConfigPlayerCountFields()

    elseif event_source == "input" then
      -- Game master's auth token

      if id == gameConfig_createGameAuthToken_id then
        GAME_CONFIG.auth_token = value or ""
      end

      -- Player auth tokens
      if metadata[2] == "player-auth-token" then
        GAME_CONFIG.player_auth_tokens[tonumber(metadata[3])] = value
        resolved = true

      -- Bot turn timeout
      elseif id == gameConfig_botTurnTimeoutMsInput_id then
        GAME_CONFIG.bot_turn_timeout_ms = tonumber(value) or 0
        resolved = true

      -- Blinds
      elseif id == gameConfig_initialCostBigBlindInput_id then
        GAME_CONFIG.big_blind_cost = tonumber(value) or 0
        resolved = true
      elseif id == gameConfig_initialCostSmallBlindInput_id then
        GAME_CONFIG.small_blind_cost = tonumber(value) or 0
        resolved = true

      -- Starting chips
      elseif metadata[2] == "starting-chips" then
        if metadata[3] == "10" then
          GAME_CONFIG.starting_10_chips = tonumber(value) or 0
          resolved = true
        elseif metadata[3] == "50" then
          GAME_CONFIG.starting_50_chips = tonumber(value) or 0
          resolved = true
        elseif metadata[3] == "100" then
          GAME_CONFIG.starting_100_chips = tonumber(value) or 0
          resolved = true
        elseif metadata[3] == "500" then
          GAME_CONFIG.starting_500_chips = tonumber(value) or 0
          resolved = true
        elseif metadata[3] == "1000" then
          GAME_CONFIG.starting_1000_chips = tonumber(value) or 0
          resolved = true
        end
      end
    elseif event_source == "toggle" then
      -- Auto-start hands
      if id == gameConfig_autoStartHandsToggle_id then
        GAME_CONFIG.auto_start_hands = value == "True" and true or false
      -- Chip denominations
      elseif metadata[2] == "using-chip-denomination" then
        if     id == gameConfig_usingChipDenomination10Toggle_id then
          GAME_CONFIG.use_10_chips = "True" and true or false
          resolved = true
        elseif id == gameConfig_usingChipDenomination50Toggle_id then
          GAME_CONFIG.use_50_chips = value == "True" and true or false
          resolved = true
        elseif id == gameConfig_usingChipDenomination100Toggle_id then
          GAME_CONFIG.use_100_chips = value == "True" and true or false
          resolved = true
        elseif id == gameConfig_usingChipDenomination500Toggle_id then
          GAME_CONFIG.use_500_chips = value == "True" and true or false
          resolved = true
        elseif id == gameConfig_usingChipDenomination1000Toggle_id then
          GAME_CONFIG.use_1000_chips = value == "True" and true or false
          resolved = true
        end
        _updateGameConfigStartingChipsInputFields()
      end
    end

    if not resolved then
      log_message = logString("["..event_source.."] event-source not supported. Event originated from ["..id.."] with value of["..value.."]")
    end
    
  end

  local giving_stack_type        = params.giving_stack_type
  local receiving_stack_type     = params.receiving_stack_type
  local onFinish_params          = params.onFinish_params

  if not type(params.chips_to_move) == "table" then
    log("Invalid [chips_to_transfer] parameter provided", "ChipManager.moveChipsBetweenStacks", "[ERROR]", false, true)
    return
  end

  -- Each movement can be done 
  local promises      = {}
  local denominations = {}
  local counts        = {}
  for denomination, count in pairs(params.chips_to_move) do

      table.insert(counts, count)

    return true

    -- Empty move data. Whatever.
    onFinish_params.service.call(onFinish_params.callback, onFinish_params.args)
    return
  end

  local givable_chips = getChipsByMemo(givable_chip_data.memo)
  
  local receivable_chip_data = generateChipData(owner, receiving_stack_type)
  local receivable_chips = getChipsByMemo(receivable_chip_data.memo)
  
  local chip_offsets = CHIP_DENOMINATION_RELATIVE_POSITION

  function _getChipToMoveForDenomination(denomination)
    if not givable_chips[denomination] then
      log(giving_stack_type.." has no valid reference of a $"..denomination.." chip that can be referenced", "ChipManager.moveChipsBetweenStacks", "ChipManager.moveChipsBetweenStacks", "[ERROR]", false, true)
      return
    end
    for chip_reference in givable_chips[denomination] do
      if chip_reference then
        return chip_reference
      end
    end
  end

  -- TODO: Adjust exchange zone to a position for bots
  local receiving_stack_zone = nil
  if string.lower(receiving_stack_type) == "stack" then
    receiving_stack_zone = owner.zones.stack_zone
  elseif string.lower(receiving_stack_type) == "bet" then
    receiving_stack_zone = owner.zones.bet_zone
  elseif string.lower(receiving_stack_type) == "exchange" then
    if owner.user_type == "bot" then
      receiving_stack_zone = BotChipExchangeStackZone
    else
      receiving_stack_zone = ChipExchangeStackZone
    end
  elseif string.lower(receiving_stack_type) == "pot" then
    receiving_stack_zone = PotStackZone
  end

  function _getDestinationForDenomination(denomination)
    if receivable_chips[denomination] then
      for chip_reference in receivable_chips[denomination] do
        if chip_reference then
          return chip_reference
        end
      end
    end
    if type(receiving_stack_zone) == "userdata" then
      return receiving_stack_zone.positionToWorld(chip_offsets[denomination])
    elseif type(receiving_stack_zone) == "table" then
      return {
        x = receiving_stack_zone.x + chip_offsets[denomination].x,
        y = receiving_stack_zone.y + chip_offsets[denomination].y,
        z = receiving_stack_zone.z + chip_offsets[denomination].z
      }
    end
  end

  function _moveChipsForPromise(index)
    local denomination = denominations[index]
    local count        = counts[index]

    -- Early return if there's no chips left to move
    if count == 0 then
      promises[index] = true
      return
    end

    -- Get the chips being moved
    local chip_reference = _getChipToMoveForDenomination(denomination)
    -- Where the chips will move to
    local destination    = _getDestinationForDenomination(denomination)

    if not chip_reference then
      log("Could not find $"..denomination.." chips to move in "..giving_stack_type.." for "..owner.display_name.." ("..owner.user_id..")", "ChipManager.moveChipsBetweenStacks", "[ERROR]", false, true)
      return
    end

    local transferChips_params = {
      chips_to_transfer = chip_reference,
      destination       = destination,
      count             = count,
      new_name          = receivable_chip_data.name,
      new_memo          = receivable_chip_data.memo,
      onFinish_params   = {
        service  = self,
        callback = "unlockAssociativeMutex",
        args     = denomination
      }
    }
    lockAssociativeMutex(denomination)
    local number_of_chips_moved = transferChips(transferChips_params)
    counts[index] = count - number_of_chips_moved

    Wait.condition(
      function()
        givable_chips    = getChipsByMemo(givable_chip_data.memo)
        receivable_chips = getChipsByMemo(receivable_chip_data.memo)
        _moveChipsForPromise(index)
      end,
      function() return isAssociativeMutexUnlocked(denomination) end
    )
  end
  
  for i = 1, #promises do
    _moveChipsForPromise(i)
  end

  Wait.condition(
    function()
      onFinish_params.service.call(onFinish_params.callback, onFinish_params.args)
    end,
    _promisesFulfilled
  )
end

function exchangeChips(params)

  local giving_chips_mutex_index     = "exchangeChips -- moving the give chips"
  local exchanging_chips_mutex_index = "exchangeChips -- deleting the given chips and spawning the receive chips"
  local receiving_chips_mutex_index  = "exchangeChips -- moving the receive chips"

  -- The first move is give->receive, the second move is receive->give.
  local giving_stack_type    = "stack"
  local receiving_stack_type = "exchange"

  -- Unpacked params
  local owner           = params.owner
  local give_chips      = params.chips_to_exchange.give
  local receive_chips   = params.chips_to_exchange.receive
  local onFinish_params = params.onFinish_params

  --[[
    The exchange process for bots is broken into 4 steps that allow each
    process to be encapsulated thanks to execution control flow:
      1. Move the given chips
      2. Delete the given chips and spawn in the received chips
      3. Move the received chips
      4. Invoke the onFinish callback  
  ]] 
  lockAssociativeMutex(giving_chips_mutex_index)
  lockAssociativeMutex(exchanging_chips_mutex_index)
  lockAssociativeMutex(receiving_chips_mutex_index)

  -- Step 1: Move given chips
  -- The first thing to happen is moving the chips being exchanged to their
  -- designated zone
  local give_moveChipsBetweenStacks_params = {
    owner = owner,
    giving_stack_type = giving_stack_type,
    receiving_stack_type = receiving_stack_type,
    chips_to_move = give_chips,

    onFinish_params = {
      service  = self,
      callback = "unlockAssociativeMutex",
      args     = giving_chips_mutex_index
    }
  }
  moveChipsBetweenStacks(give_moveChipsBetweenStacks_params)

  
  -- Step 2: Delete given chips and spawn in the received chips
  -- This list will contain all the information for the chips we need to create
  local exchange_chip_data = generateChipData(owner, receiving_stack_type)
  local spawnChips_params_list = generateSpawnChipsParameters({
    name        = exchange_chip_data.name,
    memo        = exchange_chip_data.memo,
    origin_zone = BotChipExchangeStackZone,
    chips       = receive_chips
  })
  Wait.condition(
    function()
      -- The given chips are deleted and the received chips are spawned
      local given_chips = getChipsByMemo(exchange_chip_data.memo)
      for _, chip_references in pairs(given_chips) do
        for chip_reference in chip_references do
          if chip_reference then chip_reference.destruct() end
        end
      end
      for spawnChips_params in spawnChips_params_list do
        spawnChips(spawnChips_params)
      end

      -- Need to wait at least 1 frame for the game to fully destruct the given chips
      -- Once that guarantee is realized we can mark spawning chips as complete
      Wait.frames(
        function()
          unlockAssociativeMutex(exchanging_chips_mutex_index)
        end,
        1
      )
    end,
    function() return isAssociativeMutexUnlocked(giving_chips_mutex_index) end
  )

  -- Step 3: Move the received chips
  -- Once the exchange has happened, the received chips are moved to the bot's stack
  local receive_moveChipsBetweenStacks_params = {
    owner                = owner,
    giving_stack_type    = receiving_stack_type,
    receiving_stack_type = giving_stack_type,
    chips_to_move        = receive_chips,

    onFinish_params      = {
      service  = self,
      callback = "unlockAssociativeMutex",
      args     = receiving_chips_mutex_index
    }
  }
  Wait.condition(
    function()
      
      -- There's an issue where, when chips are stacked, the reference for one of the
      -- chips that is destroyed when the stack is formed lingers. I don't know if ther
      -- is a specified time/frame i should wait, but around 0.75 seconds seems to be
      -- enough time on my system for it to figure itself out.
      Wait.time(
        function() moveChipsBetweenStacks(receive_moveChipsBetweenStacks_params) end,
        0.75
      )
    end,
    function() return isAssociativeMutexUnlocked(exchanging_chips_mutex_index) end
  )

  -- Step 4: Invoke the onFinish callback
  -- Everything is done. All that's left is to give control back to the caller.
  Wait.condition(
    function()
      onFinish_params.service.call(onFinish_params.callback, onFinish_params.args)
    end,
    function() return isAssociativeMutexUnlocked(receiving_chips_mutex_index) end
  )
end

function moveBetsToPot(onFinish_params)
  -- Completion of this function determined is when all players with active bets have had their bets collected
  local mutex_indices = {}
  function _allMutexesReleased()
    for mutex_index in mutex_indices do
      if not isAssociativeMutexUnlocked(mutex_index) then return false end
    end
    return true
  end

  -- All players in/out are checked. Out players won't have a bet, but if they did, it's collected.
  local players = PlayerManager.call("getPlayers")

  -- Execution of a player's bets being collected occurs after the previous player's bet has been collected.
  -- This allows chips to be moved quickly without having to manage collapsing multiple references into one.
  local previous_mutex_index = nil
  for player in players do
    -- This index can be arbitrary
    local mutex_index = player.user_id.." collecting bet"

    -- If the player doesn't have any chips betted then they will be skipped.
    local player_has_betted_chips = false
    -- The data we get from the getChipsByMemo is { [denomination] = {Object, ...} } which 
    -- needs to be mapped to { [denomination] = int }
    local chips_to_move = {}
    local betted_chips = getChipsByMemo( generateChipData(player, "bet").memo )
    for denomination, chip_references in pairs(betted_chips) do
      chips_to_move[denomination] = 0
      for chip_reference in chip_references do
        chips_to_move[denomination] = chips_to_move[denomination] + math.abs(chip_reference.getQuantity())
        player_has_betted_chips = true
      end
    end

    if player_has_betted_chips then
      -- Since this loop executes synchronously we can ensure each coroutine will execute only when
      -- the previous coroutine has finished
      lockAssociativeMutex(mutex_index)
      table.insert(mutex_indices, mutex_index)
      local locally_scoped_previous_mutex_index = previous_mutex_index -- need a locally scoped variable for a later comparison
      previous_mutex_index = mutex_index

      Wait.condition(
        function()
          moveChipsBetweenStacks({
            owner = player.user_id,
            giving_stack_type = "bet",
            receiving_stack_type = "pot",
            chips_to_move = chips_to_move,
            onFinish_params = {
              service = self,
              callback = "unlockAssociativeMutex",
              args = mutex_index
            }
          })
        end,
        function()
          -- If there is no previous mutex index assigned then this is the first coroutine to run
          if locally_scoped_previous_mutex_index == nil then return true end
          -- Once the previous mutex index is released then it is this coroutine's turn
          if not isAssociativeMutexUnlocked(locally_scoped_previous_mutex_index) then return false end
          return true
        end
      )
    end
  end

  Wait.condition(
    function() onFinish_params.service.call(onFinish_params.callback, onFinish_params.args) end,
    _allMutexesReleased
  )
end

    onFinish_params = {
      service   = <Scripting Zone>,
      callback  = string (function name in service's script),
      args      = table (arguments to pass to callback)
    }

function startPlayerTurn(params)
  local player = getPlayerById(params.data.player_id)
  log({"Starting " .. player.display_name.."'s turn"}, "PlayerManager.startPlayerTurn", "[INFO]", false, true)
  broadcastToAll(player.display_name.."'s turn", player.color)

  lockPlayerTurnMutex()

  if player.user_type == "bot" then
    local animate_player_params = {
      data = params.data,
      onFinish_params = PlayerTurn_onFinish_params
    }
    animatePlayerAction(animate_player_params)
  else

      player,
      params.data.current_round,
      params.data.current_stack_amount,
      params.data.minimum_chip_in
    )
    
  end

  Wait.condition(
    function() endPlayerTurn(params) end,

  )

function revealActiveHands(onFinish_params)
  log("Revealing active hands")
  local promises = {}
  local players_that_must_reveal = {}
  for player in PLAYERS do
    log(player.display_name.." has state "..player.state)
    if player.state ~= "fold" and player.state ~= "out" then
      player.state = "show"
      table.insert(promises, false)
      table.insert(players_that_must_reveal, player)
    end
  end

  function _promisesAreFulfilled()
    for promise_fulfilled in promises do
      if not promise_fulfilled then
        return false
      end
    end
    return true
  end

  if #promises == 0 then
    log("No players have an active hand", "PlayerManager.revealActiveHands", "[ERROR]", false, true)
    return
  end

  if #promises == 1 then
    log("Only one player is active. No reveal required.")
    onFinish_params.service.call(onFinish_params.callback, onFinish_params.args)
    return
  end

  log(#players_that_must_reveal.." players must reveal their cards.")
  
  for i, player in ipairs(players_that_must_reveal) do
    local index = i
    local mutex_key = "Show_"..index
    
    -- NOTE: Disabled until i add a way to track when a player has shown their hand

        }
      }
      DeckManager.call("movePlayerCardsToReflectIntent", params)

      Wait.condition(
        function() log("Unlocking "..mutex_key) promises[index] = true end,
        function() return isAssociativeMutexUnlocked(mutex_key) end
      )
    -- end
    
    -- Todo: Figure out how to ensure players have shown their cards.
    -- That'll be fun :^)
  end

  Wait.condition(
    function() onFinish_params.service.call(onFinish_params.callback, onFinish_params.args) end,
    _promisesAreFulfilled

--[[
  Setting the table from an existing state.

  The PLAYERS table will look like this after this function is ran:
  {
    {
      user_id = string,
      display_name = string,
      user_type = string,
      color = string,
      position = int,
      state = string,
      hole = {

      }
    },

  }
--]]
function setPlayers(players)

  log("Setting players from table state")
  PLAYERS = {}

  -- Upload players in the game to the global variable
  for _, player in ipairs(players) do
    PLAYERS[#PLAYERS+1] = player
  end
  -- Order players by their position so we can iterate through them naturally
  table.sort(PLAYERS, function(a, b) return a.position < b.position end)

  -- Figuring out which seats players can occupy. If there's less
  -- than 8, then players should be centered in front of the dealer.
  local starting_seat = math.floor(#SEATS/2) - math.floor(#players/2 - 1)
  for player in PLAYERS do
    player.color = SEATS[player.position + starting_seat]
    player.zones = PlayerZones[player.color]
    starting_seat = starting_seat

  -- Give player chips and put their bets (if any) forward
    local player_chips = ChipManager.call("initializeChipsForPlayer", player)
    player.stack = player_chips.stack
    player.bet = player_chips.current_bet
  end

  -- Seat present players to their assigned position
  -- This gets players that are present IN the game
  local tts_player_instances = Player.getPlayers() --TTS's PlayerManager instance
  for instance in tts_player_instances do
    local player = getPlayerById(instance.steam_id)
    if player then
      instance.changeColor(player.color)
    end
  end

  return true
end

function updatePlayerStackAndBet(player)
  -- Resetting these fields because some TTS operations can cause the existing references
  -- to be destroyed.
  resetPlayerStack(player)
  resetPlayerBet(player)

  local chips_for_this_player = {}
-- Getting a reference to all chip stacks on the table for this player
  for object in getObjects() do
    if ChipManager.call("isChip", object) and string.find(object.memo, player.user_id) then
      table.insert(chips_for_this_player, object)
    end
  end
  -- Chips in the PotZone are part of the player's bet
  -- Chips outside of the PotZone are part of the stack
  for chip in chips_for_this_player do
    -- Had a weird issue with assignment of nil to not removing an association
    local value = chip.getValue() * math.abs(chip.getQuantity())
    if string.find(chip.memo, "(Bet)") then
      table.insert(player.bet[tostring(chip.getValue())], chip)
      player.bet_value = player.bet_value + value
    else
      table.insert(player.stack[tostring(chip.getValue())], chip)
      player.stack_value = player.stack_value + value
    end
  end
end

--[[
  Creates a persistent observer that invokes a callback whenever the 
  observed field changes.

  The observer self-terminates and disposes once the `continue_observing`
  field is set to false.

  params = {
    getValue     = func <any>,
    onChange     = func <void>,
    continue_observing = boolean
  }
]]
function _startMutationObserver(params)
  local getValue           = params.getValue
  local onChange           = params.onChange
  local old_value          = getValue()

  Wait.condition(
    function()
      if params.continue_observing then
        onChange()
        _startMutationObserver(params)
      end
    end,
    function() return old_value ~= getValue() or not params.continue_observing end
  )
end

  CURRENT_BET_VALUE = 0

    CURRENT_BET_VALUE = CURRENT_BET_VALUE + chip.getValue() * math.abs(chip.getQuantity())
  end
end

--[[
  We can determine what the player is doing with their cards
  by their location and rotation.
]]
function updateCurrentPlayerCardPosition()
  if CURRENT_PLAYER == nil then return end

  if #CURRENT_PLAYER.hole ~= 2 then
    CURRENT_PLAYER_CARD_POSITION = CARD_POSITION.no_cards
    log("No cards")
    return
  end

  local number_of_cards_in_hand = 0
  -- Check if cards are in the player's hand
  for object in CURRENT_PLAYER.zones.hand_zone.getObjects() do
    if object.type == "Card" then
      for card in CURRENT_PLAYER.hole do
        if card == object then
          number_of_cards_in_hand = number_of_cards_in_hand + 1
          break
        end
      end
    end
  end

  if number_of_cards_in_hand == 2 then 
    CURRENT_PLAYER_CARD_POSITION = CARD_POSITION.in_hand
    log("In hand")
    return
  end

  local number_of_cards_face_down = 0
  local number_of_cards_face_up   = 0
  for card in CURRENT_PLAYER.hole do
    if card.is_face_down then number_of_cards_face_down = number_of_cards_face_down + 1
    else number_of_cards_face_up = number_of_cards_face_up + 1
    end
  end

  if number_of_cards_face_down == 2 then
    CURRENT_PLAYER_CARD_POSITION = CARD_POSITION.folded
    log("folded")
    return
  end
  if number_of_cards_face_up == 2 then
    CURRENT_PLAYER_CARD_POSITION = CARD_POSITION.showing
    log("showing")
    return
  end

  log("unknown")
  CURRENT_PLAYER_CARD_POSITION = CARD_POSITION.unknown
end

--[[
  A DTO can be derived from the where the player's cards or chips are.
]]
function updatePlayerActionDto()
  if CURRENT_PLAYER == nil then return end
  local player_action_dto = { player_id = CURRENT_PLAYER.user_id }

  player_action_dto.chips = {}
  for chip in CURRENT_CHIPS_BEING_BET do
    local denomination = tostring(chip.getValue())
    local count        = math.abs(chip.getQuantity())
    if not player_action_dto.chips[denomination] then
      player_action_dto.chips[denomination] = 0
    end
    player_action_dto.chips[denomination] = player_action_dto.chips[denomination] + count
  end

  if CURRENT_ROUND == "setup" then
    -- `all_in` is transformed to `ante` by the server if necessary
    if CURRENT_BET_VALUE == CURRENT_MINIMUM_CHIP_IN then
      -- Can only put forward up to the blind cost for the ante
      player_action_dto.intent = "ante"
    elseif CURRENT_BET_VALUE < CURRENT_MINIMUM_CHIP_IN and CURRENT_BET_VALUE == CURRENT_PLAYER_STACK_AMOUNT then
      player_action_dto.intent = "all_in"
    end
  elseif CURRENT_BET_VALUE == CURRENT_PLAYER_STACK_AMOUNT then
    player_action_dto.intent = "all_in"
  elseif CURRENT_PLAYER_CARD_POSITION == CARD_POSITION.folded then
    player_action_dto.intent = "fold"
    player_action_dto.chips = nil -- Don't bet chips if the player is folding.
  elseif CURRENT_BET_VALUE == 0 and CURRENT_MINIMUM_CHIP_IN == 0 then
    player_action_dto.intent = "check"
    player_action_dto.chips = nil
  elseif CURRENT_BET_VALUE == CURRENT_MINIMUM_CHIP_IN then
    player_action_dto.intent = "call"
  elseif CURRENT_BET_VALUE > CURRENT_MINIMUM_CHIP_IN then
    player_action_dto.intent = "raise"
  end

  PLAYER_ACTION_DTO = player_action_dto
end

function onObjectSpawn(object)
  if Deck == nil and object.type == "Deck" then
    log("Deck found!")
    Deck = object
  end
end

function onObjectDestroy(object)
  if Deck == nil then return end
  if object.guid == Deck.guid then
    log("Deck lost!")
    Deck = nil
    -- This event fires if the dealer stacks the original deck
    -- onto a different one. This happens after the onObjectSpawn
    -- event fires for the new deck, so we have to look for it.
    for object in getAllObjects() do
      if object.type == "Deck" then
        log("Deck found!")
        Deck = object
        break;
      end
    end
  end
end

--[[
  Card data is vague. We can identify a card by supplying it a
  string field (via memo) stating its rank and suite. However,
  this means that we have to either do this manually or programatically.

  In comes this function, creating all the cards in a deck (in order) and 
  supplying this meta data for reference later.

  Deck is an array of objects with the following layout:
  [{ rank = X, suite = X }, ...]
  If not provided, a new deck will be supplied.
--]]
function createDeck(deck)
    local spawn_position = self.getPosition()
    -- The first card created will become the deck
    -- Subsequent cards get added to that deck.
    
    -- Todo: if the deck is not nil, then construct a subset of
    -- card_map from the provided deck.
    local all_card_info = {}
    deck = nil
    local spawn_position = {x = 0.20, y = 1.79, z = -11.42}
    local height_increment = 0.5

    if deck == nil then
        for rank, details in pairs(card_map) do
            for suit, imageURL in pairs(details) do
                -- all_card_info[#all_card_info+1] = CardInfo:new(rank, suite) 
                local spawned_card = spawnObject({
                    type = "Card",
                    position = {spawn_position.x, spawn_position.y, spawn_position.z},
                    rotation = {0, 180, 180},
                    scale = {1, 1, 1}
                })

                local cardProperties = {
                    face = imageURL,
                    back = Back_of_Card,
                    sideways = false,
                    width = 1,
                    height = 1,
                    number = 1
                }

                spawned_card.setCustomObject(cardProperties)
                spawned_card.memo = rank .. suit
                spawned_card.addTag("Discard")
                spawned_card.addTag("Street1")
                spawned_card.addTag("Street2")
                spawned_card.addTag("Street3")
                spawned_card.addTag("Street4")
                spawned_card.addTag("Street5")

                spawn_position.y = spawn_position.y + height_increment
            end
        end

    end
end

--[[
    If a deck is in the zone, this function will return an ordered 
    array of all the cards in the deck.
--]]
function getCardsInDeck()
  if Deck == nil then
    broadcastToAll("Error: Could not find deck!\nMove deck to dealer zone if one exists.", {r=0, g=1, b=1})
    return nil -- We don't have a deck to get the card order of
  end

  -- https://stackoverflow.com/questions/1426954/split-string-in-lua
  function split_memo(card)
    local t = {}
    for k,_ in string.gmatch(card.memo, ".") do
      t[#t+1] = k
    end
    return {
      rank = string.byte(t[1]),
      suit = string.byte(t[2])
    }
  end

  local cards_in_deck = Deck.getObjects()
  local card_order = {}
  for card, _ in cards_in_deck do
    card_order[card.index+1] = split_memo(card)
  end
  log(JSON.encode(card_order))

  return nil
end

--[[
  deal_data: {
    -- "rank" and "suite" are ascii char values. The Go server we 
    -- use stores these fields as "runes" which are essentially chars.
    -- We need to convert these to characters in order to locate cards.
    cards: [{rank: int, suite: int}, {rank: int, suite: int}, ...]
    
    position: {x: float, y: float, z: float} -- Where to put the cards after they're removed from the deck

    is_face_up: bool
  }
]]
function dealCards(deal_data)
  local cards_to_find = {}
  for card in deal_data.cards do
    cards_to_find[#cards_to_find+1] = string.char(card.rank) .. string.char(card.suit)
  end

  local cards_dealt = {}

  for card_to_find in cards_to_find do
    for card in Deck.getObjects() do
      if card.memo == card_to_find then

        local card_instance = Deck.takeObject({
          guid = card.guid,
          position = deal_data.position,
          -- Only rotation value that matters is Y
          -- if the rotation has the card face up it can be seen before it should
          rotation = {0, deal_data.rotation.y, 180},
          callback_function = function(taken_card)
            -- Flipping in this callback makes sure the cards arrive to their
            -- destination before becoming visible (e.g. the player's hand)
            if deal_data.is_face_up then taken_card.flip() end
          end
        })
        table.insert(cards_dealt, card_instance)
      end
    end
  end
  return cards_dealt
end

--[[
    All fields are optional. Sets the street and discard pile.
    street_data: {
        discard: [{rank: int, suite: int}], ...}]   // (Max 3)
        street: [{rank: int, suite: int}, ...] // (Max 5)
    }
--]]
function setStreet(table)

  local street_data = table.street

  if street_data.discard then
    local deal_data = {
      cards = {},
      position = DiscardPosition,
      is_face_up = false
    }
    for card_data in street_data.discard do
      deal_data.cards[#deal_data.cards+1] = string.char(card_data.rank) .. string.char(card_data.suite)
    end
    dealCards(deal_data)
  end

  if street_data.street then
    local street_index = 1
    for card_data in street_data.street do
      if (street_index > #StreetPositions) then
        log("Error: More cards in the street than can exist.")
        log(street_data.street)
        break
      end
      dealCards({
        cards = {card_data},
        position = StreetPositions[street_index],
        is_face_up = true
      })
      street_index = street_index + 1
    end
  end
end

function dealHand(onFinish_params)
  Global.call("disableCardStacking")
  -- Internal mutex for delaying the dealing of another card until the preceding
  -- one has finished moving
  local card_in_transit = false
  function noCardInTransit() return not card_in_transit end

  local deal_starts_from = PlayerManager.call("getPlayerByPosition", BlindManager.getVar("DealerButtonPosition"))
  log("Deal starts from: " .. deal_starts_from.display_name)
  local current_player_being_dealt = PlayerManager.call("getNextValidPlayer", deal_starts_from)

  function dealCardToPlayer()
    if #current_player_being_dealt.hole >= 2 then
      --[[
        dealHand returns much sooner than the final card is dealt.
        onFinish_params contains information for a function to call when this
        function's operations complete, which i'm using to disable a mutex set
        in TurnManager
      --]] 
      
      Wait.condition(
        function()
          onFinish_params.service.call(onFinish_params.callback)
        end,
        noCardInTransit
      )
      return
    end

    card_in_transit = true
    local dealt_card = Deck.takeObject({
      position = current_player_being_dealt.zones.hand_zone.getPosition(),
      rotation =  {x=0, y=current_player_being_dealt.zones.hand_zone.getRotation().y, z=180},
      top = true,
      smooth = true,
      callback_function = function(card)
        card.flip()
        card_in_transit = false
      end
    })
    PlayerManager.call("addCardToPlayerHole", {position = current_player_being_dealt.position, card = dealt_card})
    current_player_being_dealt = PlayerManager.call("getNextValidPlayer", current_player_being_dealt)

    Wait.condition(
      dealCardToPlayer,
      noCardInTransit
    )
  end

  function dealCards()
    -- Burn top card
    -- card_in_transit = true
    -- Deck.takeObject({
    --   position = DiscardPosition,
    --   flip = false,
    --   top = true,
    --   callback_function = function()
    --     card_in_transit = false
    --   end
    -- })

    Wait.condition(
      dealCardToPlayer,
      noCardInTransit
    )
  end

  dealCards()

  return true
end

function burnCard()
  lockExternalScriptMutex()
  Deck.takeObject({
    position = DiscardPosition,
    rotation =  {x=0, y=0, z=180},
    top = true,
    callback_function = function(card)
      unlockExternalScriptMutex()
    end
  })
end

function dealFlop(onFinish_params)
  -- burn one card
  -- deal 3 cards onto the street 
  burnCard()

  local index = 1
  for i=1, 3 do
    local pos = i
    Wait.condition(
      function()
        lockExternalScriptMutex()
        Deck.takeObject({
          position = StreetPositions[pos],
          rotation = {0, 0, 180},
          top = true,
          callback_function = function(card)
            unlockExternalScriptMutex()
            card.flip()
            index = index + 1
          end
        })

        if index == 3 then
          Wait.condition(
            function()
              onFinish_params.service.call(onFinish_params.callback, onFinish_params.args)
            end,
            isExternalScriptMutexUnlocked
          )
        end
      end,
      function() return isExternalScriptMutexUnlocked() and index == i end
    )
  end
end

function gatherCards(onFinish_params)
  Global.call("enableCardStacking")
  local cards_on_table = {}
  -- Hopin that the group method will group to the first index in the collection provided
  if Deck then table.insert(cards_on_table, Deck) end
  for object in getObjects() do
    if object.type == "Card" or object.type == "Deck" then
      table.insert(cards_on_table, object)
    end
  end
  
  PlayerManager.call("removeCardsFromPlayerHoles")

  local collection = group(cards_on_table)
  collection[1].setPositionSmooth(DeckZone.getPosition(), false, false)
  collection[1].setRotationSmooth(DeckZone.getRotation(), false, false)

  Wait.time(
    function() onFinish_params.service.call(onFinish_params.callback, onFinish_params.args) end,
    GATHER_CARDS_DELAY
  )
end

--[[
  params = {
    player = <Player>,
    onFinish_params = {
      service  = <Scripting Zone>,
      callback = string,
      args     = table
    }
  }
]]
function movePlayerCardsToReflectIntent(params)
  local player = params.player
  local onFinish_params = params.onFinish_params

  

  if player.state ~= "fold" and player.state ~= "show" then  
    -- Nothing to do, issue the callback
    onFinish_params.service.call(onFinish_params.callback, onFinish_params.args)
    return
  end

  local blind_zone = player.zones.blind_zone -- Safest place to lay cards
  local rotation   = player.zones.blind_zone.getRotation()
  local scale      = player.zones.blind_zone.getScale()

  local card_in_transit = true
  function noCardInTransit() return not card_in_transit end

  local is_face_up = player.state ~= "fold"
  local positionY = player.zones.blind_zone.getPosition().y
  local positions = {
    blind_zone.positionToWorld({-1/scale.x, -positionY, 0}),
    blind_zone.positionToWorld({1/scale.x, positionY, 0})
  }
  local index = 1
  card_in_transit = true
  for card in player.hole do
    if not is_face_up then card.flip() end
    local position = positions[index]
    Wait.time(
      function()
        card.use_hands = false
        card.setPositionSmooth(position, false, true)
        Wait.time(function() card.use_hands = true end, 1)
      end,
      0.5
    )
    index = index + 1
  end

  Wait.time(
    function()
      card_in_transit = false
    end,
    1.2
  )

  Wait.condition(
    function() onFinish_params.service.call(onFinish_params.callback, onFinish_params.args) end,
    noCardInTransit
  )
end

--[[
  Sets the order of the deck in play.

  params = {
    deck_order      = {
      1: \d{1,2}[s|h|c|d],
      ...
      52: \d{1,2}[s|h|c|d]
    },

    onFinish_params = {
      service  = <Scripting Zone>,
      callback = string,
      args     = any
    }
  }
]]
function setDeckOrder(params)
  local onFinish_params = params.onFinish_params
 
  CardOrder = params.deck_order

  local unordered_cards = {}
  function _findCardByMemo(memo)
    for card in unordered_cards do
      if card.memo == memo then return card end
    end
    log("\n[ERROR]\nDeckManager.setDeckOrder:\nFailed to find card with memo: "..memo)
  end

  --[[
    TODO:
    There are 2 main concerns with setting the order of the deck:
      1. The deck cannot be re-ordered without taking the cards 
        out of the deck.
      2. The built-in `spread()` function forces the cards face
        up when splayed.

      The first issue isn't a major concern--I can flip the cards
      before re-creating the deck to obscure the order they enter
      the deck.
      The second issue is the crux--when grouping the cards, I can
      specify the order, but not the location of where the group
      forms. The group forms at the bottom of the deck; a sharp-
      eyed participant can feasibly identify which card is at the
      bottom of the deck, giving them additional information they
      shouldn't have.

      There are a couple options I have to remedy this:
        1. Use `attachHider` or `setHiddenFrom` to obscure the 
         deck and cards from all players before spreading.
        --> (Currently using this approach)

        2. Re-implement the `spread()` function to splay out cards
          face-down. (Last resort)
  ]]
  local hide_from_table = PlayerManager.call("getSeats")
  local sort_deck_parameters = {
    {
      func = function()
        Deck.shuffle()
      end,
      post_delay_seconds = 0.18,
      log_message = "Shuffling deck to obscure previously dealt cards"
    },
    {
      func = function()
        Deck.setPositionSmooth(
          DeckSpreadZone.getPosition(), false, true
        )
        Deck.setRotationSmooth(
          DeckSpreadZone.getRotation(), false, true
        )
      end,
      post_delay_seconds = 0.5,
      log_message = "Moving deck to spread zone."
    },
    {
      func = function()
        -- This should solve any concern of players being able to 
        -- get any more information out of the deck being spread 
        -- without reimplementing the spread function.
        Deck.setHiddenFrom(hide_from_table) -- Hide the deck before it is flipped by default spread
        unordered_cards = Deck.spread(0.6)
        for card in unordered_cards do
          card.setHiddenFrom(hide_from_table) -- Hide the cards (1 frame) after the spread function is called.
        end
      end,
      post_delay_seconds = 2.4,
      log_message = "Spreading deck"
    },
    {
      func = function()
        -- For some reason, spread puts cards face up
        for card in unordered_cards do
          card.flip()
        end
      end,
      post_delay_seconds = 0.5,
      log_message = "Flipping exposed cards"
    },
    {
      func = function()
        local card_to_move = _findCardByMemo(CardOrder[#CardOrder])
        -- Preceeding the group(...) operation with this causes the deck to
        -- form in the center of the table. Not sure why--I think it has to
        -- do with interrupting the movement--since it isn't instantaneous.
        -- But happy side-effect: the deck forms in a consistent location.
        -- If I want the deck to form elsewhere, the post_delay_seconds will 
        -- need to be increased.
        card_to_move.setPosition({0,0,0})
      end,
      post_delay_seconds = 0.00,
      log_message = "Moving bottom card to a consistent position"
    },
    {
      func = function()
        local ordered_cards = {}
        -- Because the first index is where the group is formed, the last must 
        -- be where the stack is formed, and the first card is the last added
        for i=#CardOrder, 1, -1 do
          local rank_suit = CardOrder[i]
          table.insert(ordered_cards, _findCardByMemo(rank_suit))
        end
        group(ordered_cards)
      end,
      post_delay_seconds = 0.75,
      log_message = "Sorting deck by card order."
    },
    {
      func = function()
        Deck.setPositionSmooth(
          DeckZone.getPosition(), false, true
        )
        Deck.setRotationSmooth(
          DeckZone.getRotation(), false, true
        )
      end,
      post_delay_seconds = 0.5,
      log_message = "Returning deck to dealer."
    },
    {
      func = function()
        onFinish_params.service.call(onFinish_params.callback, onFinish_params.args)
      end,
      post_delay_seconds = 0,
      log_message = "Releasing caller mutex"
    }
  }

  Wait.frames(
    function()
      local index = 1
        for i=1, #sort_deck_parameters do
          local setup_index = i
          Wait.condition(
            function()
              -- Unwrapping
              local func               = sort_deck_parameters[index].func
              local post_delay_seconds = sort_deck_parameters[index].post_delay_seconds
              local log_message        = sort_deck_parameters[index].log_message
              
              log(log_message)
              func()
              
              Wait.time(
                function()
                  index = index + 1
                end,
                post_delay_seconds
              )
            end,
            function() return index == setup_index end
          )
        end
    end,

--[[
  Various things happen at the start and end of each round.
  The server defines 6 round types:
    1. setup
    2. pre_flop
    3. flop
    4. turn
    5. river
    6. completed
  
  Actions taken upon the start and end of a round depend on the round type:
    1. setup - nothing
    2. pre_flop:
        start: deal cards to players
        end: collect any bets into the pot
    3. flop:
        start: reveal the first 3 cards of the street
        end: collect any bets into the pot
    4. turn:
        start: reveal the 4th card of the street
        end: collect any bets into the pot
    3. river:
        start: reveal the 5th card of the street
        end: collect any bets into the pot and reveal cards in player's hands
    3. completed:

local DeckManager
local EventBus
local PlayerManager
local PotManager

  inferred via the start of a new round.
]]
local CURRENT_ROUND_TYPE

local ROUND_START_FUNC_MAP
local ROUND_END_FUNC_MAP

function init(params)
  ChipManager   = params.Services.ChipManager
  DeckManager   = params.Services.DeckManager
  EventBus      = params.Services.EventBus
  PlayerManager = params.Services.PlayerManager
  PotManager    = params.Services.PotManager

  do -- Routing for logic based on round type received
  ROUND_START_FUNC_MAP = {
    ["setup"]     = nil,
    ["pre_flop"]  = startPreFlop,
    ["flop"]      = startFlop,
    ["turn"]      = startTurn,
    ["river"]     = startRiver,
    ["completed"] = startCompleted
  }

  ROUND_END_FUNC_MAP = {
    ["setup"]     = nil,
    ["pre_flop"]  = endPreFlop,
    ["flop"]      = endFlop,
    ["turn"]      = endTurn,
    ["river"]     = endRiver,
    ["completed"] = nil
  }
  end

  EventBus.call("subscribe", {
    event_type = "round_started",
    callback_params = {
      service  = self,
      callback = "onRoundStart"
    }
  })

  EventBus.call("subscribe", {
    event_type = "hand_payouts",
    callback_params = {
      service  = self,
      callback = "onPayout"
    }
})

  log("RoundHandler initialized")
end


do -- Config
  ROUND_START_DELAY = 2
  ROUND_END_DELAY   = 2
end


do -- Mutexes

--[[
  This mutex is for blocking while waiting for external scripts like
  DeckManager and PotManager to finish doing stuff that requires moving
  objects.
]]
local awaiting_external_script = false
function lockExternalScriptMutex() awaiting_external_script = true end
function unlockExternalScriptMutex() awaiting_external_script = false end
function isExternalScriptMutexUnlocked() return not awaiting_external_script end

ExternalScript_onFinish_params = {
  service = self,
  callback = "unlockExternalScriptMutex"
}

--[[
  This mutex is for blocking the onFinish_params callback for the EventBus
  until all external script calls are finished.

  Todo: Might be more semantically clear if I define mutexes for "start round"
  and "end round"
]]
local running_routines = false
function lockRoundHandlerMutex() running_routines = true end
function unlockRoundHandlerMutex() running_routines = false end
function isRoundHandlerMutexUnlocked() return not running_routines end

end


function onRoundStart(params)
  local data = params.data
  local onFinish_params = params.onFinish_params

  -- if not Global.getVar("GAME_STATE_LOADED") then
  --   log("Game state not loaded yet. Deferring round start...")
  --   Wait.time(
  --     function() onFinish_params.service.call(onFinish_params.callback, onFinish_params.args) end,
  --     0.1
  --   )
  --   return
  -- end

  -- If there was a preceeding round, then we need to 
  if CURRENT_ROUND_TYPE and ROUND_END_FUNC_MAP[CURRENT_ROUND_TYPE] then
    ROUND_END_FUNC_MAP[CURRENT_ROUND_TYPE]()
  end

  CURRENT_ROUND_TYPE = data.round_type
  Wait.condition(
    function()
      if ROUND_START_FUNC_MAP[data.round_type] ~= nil then
        ROUND_START_FUNC_MAP[data.round_type]()
      end

      -- If asynchronous work is taking place we have to wait until that's finished
      Wait.condition(
        function() onFinish_params.service.call(onFinish_params.callback, onFinish_params.args) end,
        isRoundHandlerMutexUnlocked
      )
    end,
    isRoundHandlerMutexUnlocked
  )

--[[
  The payout can show up whenever a round would normally end.
  We need to be able to accumulate the bets to this point and pay it out
  from the pot.
]]
function onPayout(params)
  local data = params.data
  local onFinish_params = params.onFinish_params

  CURRENT_ROUND_TYPE = "payout"
  
  -- The payout can show up as early as at the end of the pre_flop so the
  -- function map is irrelevant here. Instead we'll gather chips manually,
  -- figure out if players should show their cards, and then divvy out the
  -- pot as described in the payload.
  log("Payout occuring. Gathering remaining bets")
  gatherBets()
  
  Wait.condition(
    function()
      log("Showing cards")
      showCardsIfShowdown()

      Wait.condition(
        function()
          log("Paying out pot")
          payoutPot(data)
          
          Wait.condition(
            function() onFinish_params.service.call(onFinish_params.callback, onFinish_params) end,
            isRoundHandlerMutexUnlocked

        end,  
        isRoundHandlerMutexUnlocked

    end,
    isRoundHandlerMutexUnlocked
  )

      THE PRE_FLOP
]]

  lockExternalScriptMutex()
  
  -- Todo: if the dealer is a human, we should block until they have
  -- hit the "Deal cards" button in the deck's context menu
  DeckManager.call("dealHand", ExternalScript_onFinish_params)

  Wait.condition(
    unlockRoundHandlerMutex,
    isExternalScriptMutexUnlocked
  )
end

  gatherBets()
end

--[[
      THE FLOP
]]
function startFlop()
  lockRoundHandlerMutex()
  lockExternalScriptMutex()

  DeckManager.call("dealFlop", ExternalScript_onFinish_params)
  
  Wait.condition(
    unlockRoundHandlerMutex,
    isExternalScriptMutexUnlocked
  )
end
function endFlop()
  gatherBets()
end

--[[
      THE TURN
]]
function startTurn()
  lockRoundHandlerMutex()
  lockExternalScriptMutex()

  DeckManager.call("dealTurn", ExternalScript_onFinish_params)
  
  Wait.condition(
    unlockRoundHandlerMutex,
    isExternalScriptMutexUnlocked
  )
end
function endTurn()
  gatherBets()
end

--[[
      THE RIVER
]]
function startRiver()
  lockRoundHandlerMutex()
  lockExternalScriptMutex()

  DeckManager.call("dealRiver", ExternalScript_onFinish_params)
  
  Wait.condition(
    unlockRoundHandlerMutex,
    isExternalScriptMutexUnlocked
  )
end
function endRiver()
  gatherBets()
end

--[[
  THE COMPLETED
]]
function startCompleted()
  lockRoundHandlerMutex()
  lockExternalScriptMutex()

  DeckManager.call("gatherCards", ExternalScript_onFinish_params)

  Wait.condition(
    unlockRoundHandlerMutex,
    isExternalScriptMutexUnlocked
  )
end


-- Common routine.
function gatherBets()
  lockRoundHandlerMutex()
  lockExternalScriptMutex()
  ChipManager.call("moveBetsToPot", ExternalScript_onFinish_params)

  Wait.condition(
    unlockRoundHandlerMutex,
    isExternalScriptMutexUnlocked
  )
end

function showCardsIfShowdown()
  lockRoundHandlerMutex()
  lockExternalScriptMutex()

  PlayerManager.call("revealActiveHands", ExternalScript_onFinish_params)

  Wait.condition(
    unlockRoundHandlerMutex,
    isExternalScriptMutexUnlocked
  )
end

--[[
  The payload for payout looks like:
  [
    {
      "player_id": string,
      "chips" {
        "1000": int,
        ...
      }
    },
    ...
  ]
]]
function payoutPot(data)
  lockRoundHandlerMutex()

  if #data == 0 then
    -- Just some stupid edge case i thought of
    unlockRoundHandlerMutex()
    return
  end

  local index = 1
  for i, payout_data in ipairs(data) do
    local id = i
    local payoutChips_params = {
      player_id       = payout_data.player_id,
      chips           = payout_data.chips,
      onFinish_params = ExternalScript_onFinish_params
    }

    Wait.condition(
      function()
        lockExternalScriptMutex()
        PotManager.call("animatePayout", payoutChips_params)
        index = index + 1
      end,
      function() return isExternalScriptMutexUnlocked() and index == id end
    )
  end

  Wait.condition(
    unlockRoundHandlerMutex,
    function() return isExternalScriptMutexUnlocked() and index == #data + 1 end
  )
end
end)

--[[
  The server is the source of truth. Most of what happens in this mod is
  dictated by what data the server provides.

  Messages from the server must be validated to ensure they fit our
  expectation, processed into a usable format, then published to the 
  EventBus so subscribers can act on new information.

  The flow of control for this is delicate. The connection to the server
  must be asynchronous to the actions taken on the table. The server may 
  provide several events in the time it takes for us to present the result 
  of one.
]]

local GameStateHandler
local Logger
local EventBus
local UserRepository

function init(params)
  GameStateHandler = params.Services.GameStateHandler
  EventBus         = params.Services.EventBus
  Logger           = params.Services.ExternalLogConnection
  UserRepository   = params.Services.UserRepository

  log("ServerClientConnection initialized")
end

local awaiting_event_bus = false
function lockExternalScriptMutex() awaiting_event_bus = true end
function unlockExternalScriptMutex() awaiting_event_bus = false end
function isExternalScriptMutexUnlocked() return not awaiting_event_bus end

ServerClientListener_onFinish_params = {
  service = self,
  callback = "unlockExternalScriptMutex"
}

do -- Connection configuration

--[[
  This holds a reference to the Game_ID on the server that this table should reflect.
  This value will either be read from the host or inferred from the response when 
  creating a game.
]]
GAME_ID = nil
function getGameId() return GAME_ID end

--[[
  Connecting to the server requires a valid auth_token.
  If mine isn't in setup as a placeholder, generate your own at:
  https://bahms.org/assets/poker-admin/ (in the User Management view)

  Note: Requires a Twitch account.
]]
AUTH_TOKEN = nil

HEADERS = {}

--[[
  This mod, and the poker server it uses, are both open source. You can deploy
  or fork your own if ours doesn't meet your needs:
  https://github.com/just-jane-inc/just-poker
]]
DEFAULT_POKER_SERVICE_ENDPOINT = "https://game.bahms.org/api/poker/game/{game_id}/state/listen"
POKER_SERVICE_ENDPOINT = nil

GAME_ENDPOINT                  = "https://game.bahms.org/api/poker/game"
DEFAULT_JOIN_GAME_ENDPOINT     = "https://game.bahms.org/api/poker/game/{game_id}/player"
DEFAULT_START_GAME_ENDPOINT    = "https://game.bahms.org/api/poker/game/{game_id}/started"
USER_ENDPOINT                  = "https://game.bahms.org/api/poker/user/me"

DEFAULT_START_HAND_ENDPOINT    = "https://game.bahms.org/api/poker/game/{game_id}/hand"
START_HAND_ENDPOINT = nil

DEFAULT_DECK_ORDER_ENDPOINT    = "https://game.bahms.org/api/poker/game/{game_id}/deck"
DECK_ORDER_ENDPOINT = nil

DEFAULT_PLAYER_ACTION_ENDPOINT = "https://game.bahms.org/api/poker/game/{game_id}/action"
PLAYER_ACTION_ENDPOINT = nil
DEFAULT_CHIP_EXCHANGE_ENDPOINT = "https://game.bahms.org/api/poker/game/{game_id}/chip/exchange"
CHIP_EXCHANGE_ENDPOINT = nil

end -- Connection configuration


-- All JSON serialized messages received from polling are indexed by the order they are received.
local MESSAGE_QUEUE = {}

-- The event_queue's growth will outpace the rate at which events are processed.
-- An index
-- The index of the latest processed event
local CURRENT_EVENT_INDEX = 0
-- All parsed messages that are awaiting to be processed
local EVENT_QUEUE = {}


--[[
  Sets global variables used for connecting to a game.  

  params = {
    server_endpoint = string,
    game_id         = string,
    auth_token      = string
  }
]]
function _setup(params)
  POKER_SERVICE_ENDPOINT = string.gsub(DEFAULT_POKER_SERVICE_ENDPOINT, "{game_id}", params.game_id)
  DECK_ORDER_ENDPOINT    = string.gsub(DEFAULT_DECK_ORDER_ENDPOINT, "{game_id}", params.game_id)
  START_HAND_ENDPOINT    = string.gsub(DEFAULT_START_HAND_ENDPOINT, "{game_id}", params.game_id)
  PLAYER_ACTION_ENDPOINT = string.gsub(DEFAULT_PLAYER_ACTION_ENDPOINT, "{game_id}", params.game_id)
  CHIP_EXCHANGE_ENDPOINT = string.gsub(DEFAULT_CHIP_EXCHANGE_ENDPOINT, "{game_id}", params.game_id)
  
  GAME_ID                = params.game_id
  GameStateHandler.setVar("GAME_ID", GAME_ID)
  
  AUTH_TOKEN             = params.auth_token
  HEADERS = {["Authorization"] = "Bearer "..AUTH_TOKEN}

  MESSAGE_QUEUE          = {}
  CURRENT_EVENT_INDEX    = 1
  EVENT_QUEUE            = {}
  
  if GAME_ID == "0" then -- Debug line. If GAME_ID is 0 then we use playback data
    log("Using playback data")
    MESSAGE_QUEUE = PREFAB_EVENT_QUEUE -- DEBUG LINE
  end
end

--[[
  The server facilitates everything that happens in game (with some caveats--see end of comment)

  There are two parts to setting up a listener:
  1. Send a POST request to the server to initialize a listener.
    (The server was designed for web socket connections. This is a compromise since TTS only supports HTTP)
  2. We poll that endpoint with GET requests

  params = {
    game_id         = string,
    auth_token      = string
  }

  returns {true} if a 200 response was received
]]
function createEventListener(params)
  log("Setting up server-client connection")
  _setup(params)

  log(params)

  if GAME_ID ~= "0" then -- Debug check. If GAME_ID is 0 then we use playback data
    WebRequest.custom(
      POKER_SERVICE_ENDPOINT,
      "POST",
      true,                               -- I AM handling the response body
      "",                                 -- Body is an empty string
      HEADERS,                            -- headers
      function(instance)                  -- callback_function
        -- instance is the web request instance after we've gotten a response
        
        if instance.is_error then
          local message = "Connection failed: " .. instance.response_code .. "\n" .. instance.text
          printToColor(
            message,
            "Black",
            "Grey"
          )
          return
        else
          local response_code = instance.response_code
          local initialization_response = instance.text
          log("Listener initialized")
          _logServerMessage(initialization_response)
  
          local body = logString(instance.text)
          log("Response code: " .. response_code .. '\n' .. body, "Connecting to listener", "[INFO]", false, true)
  
          _pollEvents(1)
        end
    end)
  end

  -- pollEvents, processMessages, and processEvents should all operate independently and asynchronously.
  _processMessages(1)
  _processEvents(1)
end

--[[
  The WebRequest API has a bug that lets it run even when the scene is unloaded.
  The instance still has access to the script, so my original recursive polling
  method would continue to run until Tabletop Simulator was closed. The solution
  was to add a few fields into the surrounding scope and use the `onUpdate`
  method to ensure the scene is still active before polling again.
]]
local POLLING_FOR_NEW_EVENTS = false
local AWAITING_EVENTS_POLL_RESPONSE = false
local EVENTS_INDEX = 1

function _getNextEvent()
  local log_message = logString("Polling Event #"..EVENTS_INDEX.." ["..GAME_ID.."]".."...", "ServerClientConnection.pollEvents", "[INFO]", false, true)
  log("\n"..log_message)

  
  WebRequest.custom(
    POKER_SERVICE_ENDPOINT,
    "GET",
    true,                               -- I AM handling the response body
    nil,                                -- Data I'm sending in the body
    HEADERS,                             -- headers

    function(instance)
      -- Expected errors: 504 (server timeout) and 502 (listener closed)
      if instance.is_error then
        local error = {
          status = instance.response_code,
          error  = instance.error,
        }
        local log_message = logString(error, "ServerClientConnection.pollEvents ("..EVENTS_INDEX..")", "[ERROR]", false, true)
        log("\n"..log_message)
      end

      local response_is_not_html_or_nil = true

      if instance.response_code == 504 then
        -- 504 is sent when the server timed out our request.
        -- Tabletop Simulator's WebRequest API doesn't have a TTL, in resposne to this we just need to poll again.
      elseif instance.response_code == 502 then
        -- 502 is sent when the server no longer holds a reference for that game.
        -- This notifies us that the game is over and that we will no longer receive events for this game_id.
        local log_message = logString("Server has closed listener.", "ServerClientConnection.pollEvents ("..EVENTS_INDEX..")", "[INFO]", false, true)
        log("\n"..log_message)
        POLLING_FOR_NEW_EVENTS = false -- This will prevent further polling.
      elseif instance.response_code >= 400 then
        -- The only response codes we should be getting are 200, 502, and 504.
        local log_message = logString("Unhandled response status ("..instance.response_code..")", "ServerClientConnection.pollEvents ("..EVENTS_INDEX..")", "[CRITICAL]")
        log("\n"..log_message)
      elseif instance.text == nil or string.find(instance.text, "<html>") then
        -- The reponse body should be JSON and not have any HTML in it.
        local log_message = logString({[instance.response_code] = instance.text or "nil"}, "ServerClientConnection.pollEvents ("..EVENTS_INDEX..") Got some weird, third kind of response.", "[CRITICAL]", false, true)
        log("\n"..log_message)
        response_is_not_html_or_nil = false
      end

      if instance.response_code == 200 and response_is_not_html_or_nil then
        -- A successful status message gives us data that we may need to act on.
        -- Messages are stored to be eventually fielded by "processMessages"
        MESSAGE_QUEUE[EVENTS_INDEX] = instance.text
        _logServerMessage(instance.text)
        EVENTS_INDEX = EVENTS_INDEX + 1
      end

      AWAITING_EVENTS_POLL_RESPONSE = false
    end
  )

  AWAITING_EVENTS_POLL_RESPONSE = true
end

--[[
  Polls the server for new events.
  Adds new events to the "message_queue" to be processed.

  index = int (Where in the message_queue this web request's response is stored)
]]
function _pollEvents(index)
  if POLLING_FOR_NEW_EVENTS then
    local log_message = logString("Already polling events", "ServerClientConnection._pollEvents", "[WARNING]", false, true)
    log(log_message)
    return
  end

  local log_message = logString("Beginning to poll events for ["..GAME_ID.."]", "ServerClientConnection._pollEvents", "[INFO]", false, true)
  log(log_message)

  POLLING_FOR_NEW_EVENTS = true
  if index ~= nil then
    EVENTS_INDEX = index
  end

  _getNextEvent()
end

function onUpdate()
  if POLLING_FOR_NEW_EVENTS and not AWAITING_EVENTS_POLL_RESPONSE then
    _getNextEvent()
  end
end

--[[
  Deserializes messages into the event_queue
]]
function _processMessages(index)
  Wait.condition(
    function()
      local payload = JSON.decode(MESSAGE_QUEUE[index])
      -- once a message is decoded its reference is no longer needed
      MESSAGE_QUEUE[index] = nil
      -- Messages map to the event_queue 1-to-1.
      -- The order messages arrive from the server matters.
      EVENT_QUEUE[index] = payload
      _processMessages(index+1)
    end,
    -- Waits until there's a message to parse.
    function() return MESSAGE_QUEUE[index] ~= nil end
  )
end

--[[
  Publish events to the EventBus, blocking until the EventBus has notified
  us that all subscribers have finished processing the event.
]]
function _processEvents(index)
  --[[
    The first event may not arrive right away. Each call to this function creates a
    coroutine that waits until the payload associated with the received message is 
    decoded and it is time for this payload to be processed.
  ]]
  Wait.condition(
    function()
      local payload = EVENT_QUEUE[index]
      if payload and payload.event_type then
        local log_message = logString("Processing event #"..payload.id.." ["..payload.event_type.."]", "ServerClientConnection.processEvents", "[INFO]", false, true)
        log(log_message)
        local params = {
          event_type      = payload.event_type,
          data            = payload.data,
          onFinish_params = ServerClientListener_onFinish_params
        }
        lockExternalScriptMutex()
        -- I want a bit of delay before publishing the event to ensure
        -- that the log message prints first.
        Wait.frames(
          function() EventBus.call("publish", params) end,
          2
        )
      end

      EVENT_QUEUE[index] = false -- Handoff has happened. Free data up
      _processEvents(index+1)
      CURRENT_EVENT_INDEX = CURRENT_EVENT_INDEX + 1
    end,
    function()
      return isExternalScriptMutexUnlocked() and EVENT_QUEUE[index] ~= nil and EVENT_QUEUE[index] ~= false
    end
  )
end

--[[
  Informs the server to start the next hand.

  onFinish_params = {
    service  = <Scripting Zone>,
    callback = string,
    args     = any
  }
]]
function startNextHand(onFinish_params)
  if GAME_ID == nil then
    onFinish_params.service.call(onFinish_params.callback, {
      success = false,
      status = 0,
      body = {
        data = {
          error = "Not listening to a game",
          error_code = 67
        }
      }
    })
    return
  end

  WebRequest.custom(
    START_HAND_ENDPOINT,
    "POST",
    true,
    "{}",
    HEADERS,

    function(instance)
      -- Expected errors: 504 (server timeout) and 502 (listener closed)
      if instance.is_error then
        local error = {
          status = instance.response_code,
          error  = instance.error,
        }
        local log_message = logString(error, "ServerClientConnection.startNexthand", "[ERROR]", false, true)
        log("\n"..log_message)
      end

      if instance.response_code == 400 then
        -- Bad request. Probably called this while in the middle of another hand.
        local log_message = logString("Response status: "..instance.response_code, "ServerClientConnection.startNextHand", "[WARNING]", false, true)
        log("\n"..log_message)
        return;
      elseif instance.response_code == 504 then
        -- 504 is sent when the server timed out our request.
        local log_message = logString("Response status: "..instance.response_code.."\nRequest timed out.", "ServerClientConnection.startNextHand", "[WARNING]", false, true)
        log("\n"..log_message)
        return
      elseif instance.response_code == 502 then
        -- 502 is sent when the server no longer holds a reference for that game.
        -- This notifies us that the game is over and that we will no longer receive events for this game_id.
        local log_message = logString("Response status: "..instance.response_code.."\nGame no longer valid.", "ServerClientConnection.startNextHand", "[WARNING]", false, true)
        log("\n"..log_message)
        return
      elseif instance.response_code >= 400 then
        -- The only response codes we should be getting are 200, 502, and 504.
        local log_message = logString("Unhandled response status: "..instance.response_code, "ServerClientConnection.startNextHand", "[ERROR]", false, true)
        log("\n"..log_message)
        return
      end

      local web_response_result = {
        success = not instance.is_error,
        status_code = instance.response_code,
        body = JSON.decode(instance.text)
      }

      log("\nServerClientConnection.startNextHand\nNext hand started.\n")
      onFinish_params.service.call(onFinish_params.callback, web_response_result)
    end
  )
end

--[[
  Fetches the order of the deck for the current GAME_ID for the current hand in the deck.
  Assumes the deck being fetched is for the game being listened to.

  The response from the server, if it is JSON, is serialized and passed to the callback provided
  by the caller.

  Because WebRequest in Tabletop Simulator is not synchronous, the content of the response body cannot
  be returned at the same time the function returns. The caller's callback must accept the serialized
  response in order for this function to be useful.

  onDeckOrderReceived_params = {
    service  = <Scripting Zone>,
    callback = string 
  }
]]
function getDeckOrder(deckOrderReceived_params)
  if GAME_ID == nil then
    deckOrderReceived_params.service.call(deckOrderReceived_params.callback, nil)
    return
  end

  WebRequest.custom(
    DECK_ORDER_ENDPOINT,
    "GET",
    true,
    nil,
    HEADERS,


    function(instance)
      -- Expected errors: 504 (server timeout) and 502 (listener closed)
      if instance.is_error then
        
        if instance.status_code == 504 then
          -- 504 is sent when the server timed out our request.
          -- Tabletop Simulator's WebRequest API doesn't have a TTL, in resposne to this we just need to poll again.
          log("ServerClientConnection.getDeckOrder\n504 error on GET deck order")
          return
        elseif instance.status_code == 502 then
          -- 502 is sent when the server no longer holds a reference for that game.
          -- This notifies us that the game is over and that we will no longer receive events for this game_id.
          log("ServerClientConnection.getDeckOrder\n502 error on GET deck order")
          return
        else
          -- The only response codes we should be getting are 200, 502, and 504.
          log("ServerClientConnection.getDeckOrder\n"..instance.status_code.." error on GET deck order")
          return
        end
      end

      if instance.text == nil or string.find(instance.text, "<html>") then
        local log_message = logString({[instance.response_code] = instance.text or "nil"}, "[ServerClientConnection.getDeckOrder] Got some weird, fifth kind of response.", "[CRITICAL]", false, true)
        log("\n"..log_message)
        return
      end


      local body = JSON.decode(instance.text)

      -- A successful status message gives us data that we may need to act on.
      -- Messages are stored to be eventually fielded by "processMessages"
      deckOrderReceived_params.service.call(deckOrderReceived_params.callback, body.data)
    end
  )
end

--[[
  Made this for two reasons:
  1. Reading logs in the console provided by Rolandostar's TTS extension in
      VSCode is great for realtime monitoring, but sucks for looking back at 
      logs. There's no Ctrl+F, there's no to-file logging afaik, and there's 
      only one log channel, so all messages occupy the same terminal.
  2. I can't listen to a game with my recorder and TTS at the same time, the
      connection consumes events from the server and they aren't repeated.
      Addressing the issues in (1.) allows me to record games for playback 
      later. I've had some bugs lately with being unable to find chips, and 
      I can't tell if the issue is from a divergence in state on my end or 
      the server's.

  How it works:
  I run an ASP.NET server locally that provides two endpoints:
  GET  /                            -- Checks if the service is live.
  POST /log/{app_id}/{file}/{level} -- Logs a message to `app_id`/`file` 
                                        with the prefix of `level` 
  Generally, app_id = game_id, file = trace/events.
  The POST body contains the message to log.
]]
local EXTERNAL_LOGGER_HOST = "http://localhost:5263/"

local CONNECTION_ESTABLISHED = false
local function _checkConnection()
  return WebRequest.get(
    EXTERNAL_LOGGER_HOST,
    function(instance)
      if not instance.is_error and instance.response_code == 200 then
        CONNECTION_ESTABLISHED = true
        local log_message = logString("Successfully connected to external logger", "ExternalLogConnection._checkConnection", "[INFO]", false, true)
        log("\n"..log_message)
      end
    end
  )
end

local GameStateHandler

function init(params)
  GameStateHandler = params.Services.GameStateHandler

  -- If we don't get a connection in less than a second then the
  -- server isn't live.
  _checkConnection()
  Wait.time(
    function()
      if not CONNECTION_ESTABLISHED then
        local log_message = logString("Failed to connect to external logger.", "ExternalLogConnection._checkConnection", "[INFO]", false, true)
        log("\n"..log_message)
      end
    end,
    0.75
  )
end

--[[
  If there is an established connection, formats a web request to the
  external logger. Otherwise does nothing.

  params = {
    game_id  = string, -- Denotes a folder
    file     = string, -- Denotes a file
    level    = string, -- Prefix for log level
    message  = string  -- Message to log
  }
]]
function logMessage(params)
  if not CONNECTION_ESTABLISHED then return end

  -- This isn't a great way to do this, but I don't have a 
  -- standardized way of storing state yet.
  local game_id = GameStateHandler.getVar("GAME_ID")

  local game_id = params.game_id or game_id
  local file    = params.file
  local level   = params.level
  local message = params.message

  if type(message) == "table" then
    message = JSON.encode(message)
  end

  if not (game_id and file and level and message) then
    local log_message = logString(params, "ExternalLogConnection.log\nMissing parameter", "[WARNING]", false, true)
    log(log_message)
  end

  local LOG_ENDPOINT = EXTERNAL_LOGGER_HOST.."log/"..game_id.."/"..file.."/"..level.."/"

  WebRequest.custom(
    LOG_ENDPOINT,
    "POST",
    true,
    message,
    {["Content-Type"]="text/plain"},
    function(instance)
      if instance.is_error or instance.response_code ~= 200 then
        local log_message = logString("Request denied with status code ["..instance.response_code.."]\n"..instance.text, "ExternalLogConnection.log", "[WARNING]", false, true)
        log(log_message)
        CONNECTION_ESTABLISHED = false -- If one request fails, subsequent will fail. Figure out why so this doesn't happen.
      end
    end
  )

end
end)
